# 0. What this file does

Study 5 asks whether the time Alex is said to have spent making a second work
from a first artwork changes how people judge that second work. The
registration calls that time editing time. It also asks whether editing time
changes the source penalty, the lower rating a second work gets when its first
artwork is attributed to AI.

This file carries out the ratings analyses of the registration,
`Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/Study5_AsPredicted.md`, and nothing beyond
them. It reads the two Qualtrics exports, applies the five exclusion steps of
the registration's question 6, rebuilds the long data and writes
`study5_long_with_text.csv` for the integration file. It then fits the registered
models and runs the six confirmatory tests with Holm's correction and the two
registered equivalence tests. Last, it checks each Holm verdict with a
cumulative-link model and runs the second analysis, on ratings rescaled from
0 to 1.

**Design.** Six cells between participants: source (Human or AI) crossed
with editing time (less than 1 hour, 10 hours, 100 hours), assigned once as
a unit. Within participants: modification (None, Slight, Dramatic) and image
kind (Figure or NonFigure). Each participant rates 18 second works on three
items: transformativeness, essence change and creativity.

**Source time.** The registration says that the hours spent on each first
artwork, called source time, were shown to participants but not recorded,
because the trial recorder read a field the survey had renamed. Source time
therefore enters no model in this file. Section 4 checks that the six
trial-time fields are blank in every analysed record.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# readr reads and writes the tables. dplyr, tidyr, tibble and purrr reshape
# them.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(purrr)
})

# lme4 fits the linear mixed models, regressions with an estimated adjustment
# for each participant and each source image. lmerTest adds F tests with
# Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, an approximation to the degrees of
# freedom a test in a mixed model effectively has. emmeans gives estimated
# marginal means, the model's predicted mean for each condition averaged over
# the other factors, and contrasts between them. ordinal fits the
# cumulative-link mixed models, which treat each answer as an ordered
# category rather than a number.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(emmeans)
  library(ordinal)
})

# A seed fixes the sequence of random numbers R draws, so a rerun draws the
# same numbers. 20260421 is the seed the registration names for R.
SEED <- 20260421L
set.seed(SEED)
```

## 1.2 Paths

```{r paths}
# Every path starts from this file's own folder, which is the working
# directory while the file is knitted. Five environment variables can name
# other folders:
#   STUDY5_DIR           the Study 5 folder, which holds the survey file and
#                        study5_long.csv
#   STUDY5_PROJECT_ROOT  the project root, the folder that holds Data and
#                        Analysis
#   STUDY5_OUTPUT_DIR    the folder outputs are written under, by default
#                        the Study 5 folder
#   STUDY_SHARED_R       the folder of the shared R helpers
#   STUDY3_DIR           the Study 3 folder, for the bound of section 9
# Printed paths are relative to the project root, so the output names no
# account and no folder particular to one machine.
STUDY_DIR <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("STUDY5_DIR", unset = getwd()),
                           mustWork = TRUE)
SHARED_R  <- Sys.getenv("STUDY_SHARED_R",
                        unset = file.path(STUDY_DIR, "..", "shared", "R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "fit_status.R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "qualtrics_import.R"))

PROJECT_ROOT <- find_project_root(start = STUDY_DIR,
                                  env_var = "STUDY5_PROJECT_ROOT")
OUTPUT_DIR   <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("STUDY5_OUTPUT_DIR", unset = STUDY_DIR),
                              mustWork = TRUE)

# An unblinded run writes its tables into tables/ and the long data beside
# this file, as Study 1 does. A blind run writes each into a blind_run/
# subfolder of the folder its real counterpart goes to: the tables into
# tables/blind_run/ and the long data into blind_run/. The Knit button sends
# a blind run's HTML report to blind_run/ as well (the knit line at the top
# of this file).
TAB_DIR <- if (UNBLIND) file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tables") else
  file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "tables", "blind_run")
LONG_DIR <- if (UNBLIND) OUTPUT_DIR else file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "blind_run")
dir.create(TAB_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(LONG_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
LONG_TEXT_PATH <- file.path(LONG_DIR, "study5_long_with_text.csv")

# The exports come from Data/Study 5 under the project root. The survey file
# is the .qsf in the Study 5 folder.
paths <- study_export_paths(PROJECT_ROOT, 5)
paths$qsf <- file.path(STUDY_DIR, "Final_-_AI_Copyright_-_Study_5.qsf")
BUILD_LONG   <- file.path(STUDY_DIR, "study5_long.csv")
BUILD_SCALES <- file.path(STUDY_DIR, "tables", "study5_item_scales.csv")
for (p in c(paths$values, paths$labels, paths$qsf, BUILD_LONG, BUILD_SCALES)) {
  if (!file.exists(p)) stop("Cannot find ", basename(p), ".")
}

# Study 3's registered creativity contrast, which sets the editing-time bound
# of section 9.
STUDY3_DIR <- Sys.getenv("STUDY3_DIR", unset = file.path(STUDY_DIR, "..", "Study 3"))
STUDY3_CONTRAST <- file.path(STUDY3_DIR, "tables", "study3_time_contrast_for_study5.csv")

cat("Mode:", if (UNBLIND) "unblinded" else "blind", "\n")
cat("Tables go to:", relative_path(TAB_DIR, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
cat("Long data goes to:", relative_path(LONG_TEXT_PATH, PROJECT_ROOT), "\n")
```

## 1.3 The two equivalence bounds

The registration fixes the editing-time bound before any Study 5 model is
fitted, so both bounds are set here, before the data are read. Section 9
uses them.

```{r bounds}
# (a) The editing-time bound is the absolute size of the 100 hours minus less
# than 1 hour contrast for source time on creativity in the registered Study
# 3 model. Study3_01_Quant.Rmd writes it as one row with the columns
# dimension, contrast, estimate, blind_run and usable. The file gives a bound
# only when its creativity row says blind_run FALSE and usable TRUE. A file
# that is absent, that comes from a blind run or whose fit was not usable
# gives no bound. An unblinded run then stops here, before any model is
# fitted. A blind run uses a placeholder, so that the code of section 9
# still runs.
PLACEHOLDER_BOUND <- 0.30

read_study3_bound <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(list(ok = FALSE, why = "the file is absent"))
  b <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
  if (!all(c("dimension", "estimate", "blind_run", "usable") %in% names(b))) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, why = "the file lacks the columns dimension, estimate, blind_run and usable"))
  }
  b <- b[b$dimension == "creativity", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(b) != 1 || is.na(b$estimate)) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, why = "the file does not hold one creativity estimate"))
  }
  if (!isFALSE(as.logical(b$blind_run))) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, why = "the file comes from a blind run"))
  }
  if (!isTRUE(as.logical(b$usable))) {
    return(list(ok = FALSE, why = "the file says its fit is not usable"))
  }
  list(ok = TRUE, bound = abs(as.numeric(b$estimate)),
       why = "Study 3, registered model, creativity, 100 hours minus less than 1 hour")
}

s3 <- read_study3_bound(STUDY3_CONTRAST)
if (s3$ok) {
  TIME_BOUND <- s3$bound
  TIME_BOUND_SOURCE <- s3$why
} else if (UNBLIND) {
  stop("The editing-time bound comes from Study 3, and ", s3$why, ". ",
       "Study 3 must be unblinded and run first, so that ",
       "Study 3/tables/study3_time_contrast_for_study5.csv holds its ",
       "registered creativity contrast.")
} else {
  TIME_BOUND <- PLACEHOLDER_BOUND
  TIME_BOUND_SOURCE <- paste0("PLACEHOLDER for a blind run (", s3$why,
                              "); not the registered bound")
}
cat("Editing-time bound:", TIME_BOUND, "|", TIME_BOUND_SOURCE, "\n")

# (b) The source bound is 0.224 rating points, half the 0.448-point
# creativity penalty Study 1 estimated on these images.
SOURCE_BOUND <- 0.224
cat("Source bound:", SOURCE_BOUND, "\n")
```

## 1.4 Run record

```{r run-record}
# The run record ties every output to this run. It stores the SHA-256
# checksum of each input, a 64-character fingerprint of the file's exact
# bytes, deletes the previous manifest before anything is written, and
# deletes each output's previous copy at the top of the chunk that writes
# it. The manifest written in section 12 lists every output and whether this
# run wrote it. When Study 3's contrast file gave the editing-time bound, it
# is recorded as an input too.
run <- start_run_record(
  inputs = c(values_export = paths$values,
             labels_export = paths$labels,
             survey_file   = paths$qsf,
             build_long    = BUILD_LONG,
             build_scales  = BUILD_SCALES,
             if (s3$ok) c(study3_contrast = STUDY3_CONTRAST)),
  manifest_path = file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_quant_run_manifest.csv"),
  base_dir      = OUTPUT_DIR)
write_run_inputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_quant_run_inputs.csv"))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")

if (!UNBLIND) {
  blind_notes <- file.path(unique(c(TAB_DIR, LONG_DIR)), "BLIND_RUN.txt")
  run_clear_outputs(run, blind_notes)
  for (p in blind_notes) writeLines(c(
    "Outputs of a blind run of Study5_01_Quant.Rmd and Study5_03_Integration.Rmd.",
    "Source and editing time were shuffled across participants, as one unit,",
    "before any summary or model, so no number in this folder describes the",
    "real conditions. A run with UNBLIND_STUDY5 set to TRUE writes the real",
    "outputs to tables/ and the long data to the Study 5 folder."), p)
}
```

# 2. Import

```{r import}
# Qualtrics exports each study twice. The Values export stores each answer as
# a raw choice code, the internal number Qualtrics gave the option, and the
# Labels export stores the text the participant saw. The two must list the
# same records in the same order, and read_qualtrics_pair() stops if they do
# not.
ex <- read_qualtrics_pair(paths$values, paths$labels)
cat("Records in the exports:", nrow(ex$values), "\n")

# read_item_scales() reads each rating item's answer options from the survey
# file, in the order they were shown, and leaves out questions deleted
# before launch. A rating is later scored by the position of its label in
# that list, 1 to k, because the raw choice codes are not scale positions.
scales <- read_item_scales(paths$qsf, ITEM_FAMILIES$derivative$pattern)
cat("Rating items:", nrow(scales), "| five-point:", sum(scales$k == 5),
    "| six-point:", sum(scales$k == 6), "\n")
cat("Six-point items:", paste(scales$item[scales$k == 6], collapse = ", "), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(scales) == 90,
          setequal(scales$item[scales$k == 6],
                   c("1NonFigureNoneTrans", "1NonFigureMinTrans")))

# The same items, scale lengths and option labels as the table that
# study5_build.py wrote.
build_scales <- read_csv(BUILD_SCALES, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                         na = character())
scale_check <- scales %>%
  select(item, k, anchors) %>%
  mutate(k = as.character(k)) %>%
  full_join(build_scales %>% select(item, k = k_points, anchors),
            by = "item", suffix = c("", "_build"))
stopifnot(nrow(scale_check) == 90,
          identical(scale_check$k, scale_check$k_build),
          identical(scale_check$anchors, scale_check$anchors_build))
cat("Item scales equal those of tables/study5_item_scales.csv: TRUE\n")
```

# 3. Exclusions (registration, question 6)

```{r exclusions}
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_exclusion_flow_registered.csv"),
                  file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_cell_counts_registered.csv"))

# The five steps of the registration, in its order and in its words. Each
# step returns TRUE for the records to keep. In the Values export, Status 0
# is a real response and Finished 1 a finished one.
TASK_ANSWER <- "Viewing images for a set amount of time and answering questions"
rating_cols <- rating_items(names(ex$values), "derivative")
n_ratings   <- function(v) rowSums(as.matrix(v[, rating_cols]) != "")

steps <- list(
  "1. Survey test runs" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(v$Status) == "0",
  "2. Unfinished records" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(v$Finished) == "1",
  "3. Seriousness answers other than \"Yes, I did\", blanks included" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(l$Seriousness) == "Yes, I did",
  "4. Wrong answers to \"What does 8+7 equal?\"" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(v$AttentionCheck2) == "" |
                   trim_answer(l$AttentionCheck2) == "15",
  "5. Records with no condition" =
    function(v, l) trim_answer(v$Type) != "" &
                   trim_answer(v$ArtistHr_Derivative) != ""
)
flow <- exclusion_flow(ex$values, ex$labels, steps)

# The flow, one line per step.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(flow$flow))) {
  r <- flow$flow[i, ]
  if (i == 1) cat(r$step, ":", r$n, "\n")
  else cat(r$step, ": removes", r$removed, "and leaves", r$n, "\n")
}

# The counts the registration states.
stopifnot(identical(flow$flow$n, c(259L, 259L, 242L, 226L, 225L, 223L)),
          identical(flow$flow$removed[-1], c(0L, 17L, 16L, 1L, 2L)))

# Step 4 lets a blank answer pass, and the registration says none occurs.
after3 <- exclusion_flow(ex$values, ex$labels, steps[1:3])
n_blank_arith <- sum(trim_answer(after3$values$AttentionCheck2) == "")
cat("Blank answers to the arithmetic question at step 4:", n_blank_arith, "\n")
stopifnot(n_blank_arith == 0)

# Step 5 removes two records, and the registration says neither has ratings.
after4 <- exclusion_flow(ex$values, ex$labels, steps[1:4])
no_cond <- !steps[[5]](after4$values, after4$labels)
cat("Ratings held by the records with no condition:",
    sum(n_ratings(after4$values[no_cond, ])), "\n")
stopifnot(sum(no_cond) == 2, sum(n_ratings(after4$values[no_cond, ])) == 0)

# The task attention check removes no one: all 223 answered it correctly.
stopifnot(all(trim_answer(flow$labels$AttentionCheck) == TASK_ANSWER))
cat("Correct answers to the task attention check:",
    sum(trim_answer(flow$labels$AttentionCheck) == TASK_ANSWER), "of",
    nrow(flow$labels), "\n")

write_csv(flow$flow, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_exclusion_flow_registered.csv"))

# Cell counts. The registration states them, and counts by cell are not a
# summary of any rating, so they are taken from the real labels in both
# modes.
cell_counts <- tibble(source = flow$values$Type,
                      editing_time = flow$values$ArtistHr_Derivative) %>%
  count(source, editing_time, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(source = factor(source, levels = c("Human", "AI")),
         editing_time = factor(editing_time,
                               levels = c("less than 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours"))) %>%
  arrange(source, editing_time)
print(as.data.frame(cell_counts))
stopifnot(identical(cell_counts$n, c(37L, 37L, 38L, 35L, 38L, 38L)))
write_csv(cell_counts, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_cell_counts_registered.csv"))
```

# 4. The long data

```{r long-data}
# One row per participant and rating item. reshape_ratings_long() scores
# each rating by position with score_by_position() and attaches the written
# justification that followed it.
built <- reshape_ratings_long(flow$values, flow$labels, scales, "derivative",
                              carry_values = c("Type", "ArtistHr_Derivative"))
cat("Rows:", nrow(built$long), "| answers that could not be scored:",
    nrow(built$unscored), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(built$unscored) == 0)

# This file rebuilds the long data from the exports with the shared R
# helpers. The rebuilt table must equal study5_long.csv, which
# study5_build.py writes, in every row and in every column the two share.
build_long <- read_csv(BUILD_LONG, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                       na = character())
rebuilt <- built$long %>%
  transmute(id, Type, deriv_effort = ArtistHr_Derivative, stimulus_id,
            stimulus_type, modification, dimension, item,
            rating = as.character(rating), k_points = as.character(k_points),
            rating_label, raw_choice_id, justification)
same <- identical(as.data.frame(rebuilt),
                  as.data.frame(build_long[, names(rebuilt)]))
cat("Rebuilt long data equals study5_long.csv:", same, "\n")
stopifnot(same)

# Every participant has 54 scored ratings and 54 written justifications.
per_person <- built$long %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_rated = sum(!is.na(rating)),
            n_justified = sum(justification != ""), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(per_person) == 223, all(per_person$n_rated == 54),
          all(per_person$n_justified == 54))
cat("Participants:", nrow(per_person), "| ratings:", sum(per_person$n_rated),
    "| justifications:", sum(per_person$n_justified), "\n")

# The within-participant design of registration question 4. Each participant
# sees 6 of the 10 source images, 3 with a human or humanoid figure (Figure)
# and 3 without (NonFigure), and each of the 6 at all three modification
# levels, which makes 18 second works.
design <- built$long %>%
  distinct(id, stimulus_id, stimulus_type, modification) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_sources   = n_distinct(stimulus_id),
            n_figure    = n_distinct(stimulus_id[stimulus_type == "Figure"]),
            n_nonfigure = n_distinct(stimulus_id[stimulus_type == "NonFigure"]),
            n_works     = n(), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(design$n_sources == 6), all(design$n_figure == 3),
          all(design$n_nonfigure == 3), all(design$n_works == 18))
cat("Every participant saw 6 source images (3 Figure, 3 NonFigure), each at",
    "three modification levels: 18 second works.\n")

# The six trial-time fields are blank in every analysed record, so no
# trial-level source time exists to enter a model.
time_fields <- paste0("Image", 1:6, "_Time")
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(flow$values[, time_fields]) == ""))
cat("Image1_Time to Image6_Time blank in all", nrow(flow$values), "records: TRUE\n")

# The analysis columns. image is the source image (ten of them), image_kind
# says whether it shows a human or humanoid figure, and work_id names the
# second work, one source image at one modification level. rating_01 is
# the rating rescaled from 0 to 1 for the second analysis of section 11.
long <- built$long %>%
  transmute(
    id,
    source       = Type,
    editing_time = ArtistHr_Derivative,
    image        = stimulus_id,
    image_kind   = stimulus_type,
    modification,
    work_id      = paste0(stimulus_id, "_", modification),
    dimension,
    item,
    k_points,
    rating,
    rating_01    = (rating - 1) / (k_points - 1),
    rating_label,
    response_text = justification
  )
stopifnot(nrow(long) == 12042, sum(long$k_points == 6) == 274,
          n_distinct(long$work_id) == 30, n_distinct(long$image) == 10)
cat("Ratings on the two six-point items:", sum(long$k_points == 6), "\n")
```

# 5. The blind switch

```{r blind-shuffle}
# In a blind run, source and editing time are dealt out again across
# participants as one unit, since the two together are one between-participant
# cell. Each participant receives another participant's pair of labels, and
# every cell keeps its size. The shuffle comes before any summary or model.
cells_before <- long %>% distinct(id, source, editing_time) %>%
  count(source, editing_time)
if (!UNBLIND) {
  long <- blind_shuffle(long, "id", c("source", "editing_time"), seed = SEED)
  cells_after <- long %>% distinct(id, source, editing_time) %>%
    count(source, editing_time)
  stopifnot(identical(cells_before$source, cells_after$source),
            identical(cells_before$editing_time, cells_after$editing_time),
            identical(cells_before$n, cells_after$n))
  cat("Labels shuffled across", attr(long, "blind_shuffle")$n_participants,
      "participants with seed", SEED, "; every cell keeps its size.\n")
} else {
  cat("Real labels.\n")
}
long$label_mode <- if (UNBLIND) "real" else "shuffled"

# Factor levels. Human and less than 1 hour come first.
long <- long %>%
  mutate(source       = factor(source, levels = c("Human", "AI")),
         editing_time = factor(editing_time,
                               levels = c("less than 1 hour", "10 hours", "100 hours")),
         modification = factor(modification, levels = c("None", "Slight", "Dramatic")),
         image_kind   = factor(image_kind, levels = c("NonFigure", "Figure")),
         dimension    = factor(dimension,
                               levels = c("transformativeness", "essence_change",
                                          "creativity")),
         id           = factor(id),
         image        = factor(image))
stopifnot(!anyNA(long$source), !anyNA(long$editing_time),
          !anyNA(long$modification), !anyNA(long$image_kind))
```

```{r write-long}
# The long data with the justifications, for the integration file. It
# carries the condition and the rating. In a blind run the condition columns
# are the shuffled ones, the file goes to blind_run/, and label_mode says
# "shuffled" on every row.
run_clear_outputs(run, LONG_TEXT_PATH)
write_csv(long %>% mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)), LONG_TEXT_PATH)
cat("Written:", relative_path(LONG_TEXT_PATH, PROJECT_ROOT), "|", nrow(long),
    "rows | label_mode", unique(long$label_mode), "\n")
```

# 6. The registered models

```{r models}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_lmm_fit_status.csv"),
                  file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_lmm_anova.csv"))

# The registered model, one per rating:
#   rating ~ source * editing_time * modification + image_kind
#            + (1 | id) + (1 | image)
# id is the participant and image the source image. Each factor is coded
# with sum-to-zero contrasts, in which each level is compared with the mean
# of all levels, so that a main effect in the F tests is that factor's
# effect averaged over the other factors. The fit uses restricted maximum
# likelihood (REML, the usual estimate of the variances in a mixed model)
# and the bobyqa optimizer, as in Study 1.
#
# The primary analysis drops the two six-point transformativeness items
# (registration, question 8), so every rating here is on five points.
RATINGS <- c("transformativeness", "essence_change", "creativity")
SUM_CONTRASTS <- list(source = "contr.sum", editing_time = "contr.sum",
                      modification = "contr.sum", image_kind = "contr.sum")
FIXED <- "source * editing_time * modification + image_kind"

# The two terms of the confirmatory family of section 7.
FAMILY_TERMS <- c("editing_time" = "editing time, averaged over the other factors",
                  "source:editing_time" = "source by editing time")

primary_data <- function(r) {
  long %>% filter(dimension == r, k_points == 5, !is.na(rating))
}

fit_lmm <- function(d, response) {
  f <- stats::as.formula(paste0(response, " ~ ", FIXED, " + (1 | id) + (1 | image)"))
  res <- fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(
    f, data = d, REML = TRUE, contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))
  res$data <- d
  res
}

primary <- setNames(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) fit_lmm(primary_data(r), "rating")),
                    RATINGS)

# The status of each fit: whether it stopped with an error, whether it
# converged, and whether it is singular (a variance estimated at zero). A
# fit that errored or did not converge carries no p-value or verdict.
status_row <- function(res, analysis, r, response) {
  d <- res$data
  bind_cols(tibble(analysis = analysis, rating = r,
                   model = paste0(response, " ~ ", FIXED, " + (1 | id) + (1 | image)"),
                   n_obs = nrow(d), n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
                   n_images = n_distinct(d$image)),
            res$status)
}
lmm_status <- bind_rows(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) {
  status_row(primary[[r]], "primary, five-point items", r, "rating")
}))
print(as.data.frame(lmm_status %>% select(-lme4_messages)))

# F tests for every term, type III with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.
anova_table <- function(res, analysis, r) {
  if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) {
    return(tibble(analysis = analysis, rating = r, term = names(FAMILY_TERMS),
                  num_df = NA_real_, den_df = NA_real_, F = NA_real_,
                  p = NA_real_, note = fit_note(res$status)))
  }
  a <- as.data.frame(anova(res$fit, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
  tibble(analysis = analysis, rating = r, term = rownames(a),
         num_df = a$NumDF, den_df = a$DenDF, F = a[["F value"]],
         p = na_unless_usable(a[["Pr(>F)"]], res$status),
         note = fit_note(res$status))
}
lmm_anova <- bind_rows(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) {
  anova_table(primary[[r]], "primary, five-point items", r)
}))
```

```{r models-write}
# The fit status table is completed in section 11, when the second
# analysis's fits are added, and written there.
write_csv(lmm_anova, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_lmm_anova.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(lmm_anova %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
```

The registration names no random-slope requirement for Study 5, so no model
with random slopes is fitted here.

# 7. The confirmatory family

```{r confirmatory}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_confirmatory_family.csv"))

# Six tests are confirmatory: the editing-time effect, averaged over the
# other factors, and the source-by-editing-time interaction, on each rating.
# Holm's method corrects the six together. It orders the p-values, compares
# the smallest with .05 divided by six, the next with .05 divided by five,
# and so on, stopping at the first that fails, which holds the chance of any
# false positive at .05. The correction is told the family has six members
# whatever happens, so a missing p-value never makes it lighter for the
# others.
family_rows <- function(anova_tab, status_tab, analysis) {
  anova_tab %>%
    filter(term %in% names(FAMILY_TERMS)) %>%
    mutate(test = unname(FAMILY_TERMS[term])) %>%
    left_join(status_tab %>% select(analysis, rating, converged, singular),
              by = c("analysis", "rating")) %>%
    transmute(analysis, rating = factor(rating, levels = RATINGS),
              test = factor(test, levels = FAMILY_TERMS), term,
              num_df, den_df, F, p_raw = p, converged, singular, note) %>%
    arrange(rating, test) %>%
    mutate(rating = as.character(rating), test = as.character(test),
           p_holm = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm", n = 6),
           holm_significant = p_holm < .05,
           family = "six registered tests, Holm, family-wise alpha .05",
           .after = p_raw)
}
confirmatory <- family_rows(lmm_anova, lmm_status, "primary, five-point items")
stopifnot(nrow(confirmatory) == 6)
print(as.data.frame(confirmatory %>% select(rating, test, num_df, den_df, F, p_raw,
                                            p_holm, holm_significant, converged,
                                            singular) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
write_csv(confirmatory, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_confirmatory_family.csv"))
```

# 8. Estimated marginal means

```{r emmeans}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_emmeans_editing_time.csv"),
                  file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_emmeans_source_by_modification.csv"))

# emmeans switches off Satterthwaite degrees of freedom above 3,000
# observations unless told otherwise. The registration names them, so the
# limit is raised above the size of any model here.
LMER_DF <- list(lmer.df = "satterthwaite", lmerTest.limit = 20000)

emm_of <- function(res, spec) {
  do.call(emmeans::emmeans, c(list(object = res$fit, specs = spec,
                                   data = res$data), LMER_DF))
}
emm_frame <- function(res, r, spec) {
  if (!fit_usable(res$status)) {
    return(tibble(rating = r, note = fit_note(res$status, "mean")))
  }
  s <- as.data.frame(summary(emm_of(res, spec)))
  tibble(rating = r, s) %>% rename(se = SE, ci_lo = lower.CL, ci_hi = upper.CL) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character), note = "")
}

emm_time <- bind_rows(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) {
  emm_frame(primary[[r]], r, ~ editing_time)
}))
emm_source <- bind_rows(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) {
  emm_frame(primary[[r]], r, ~ source | modification)
}))
print(as.data.frame(emm_time %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
print(as.data.frame(emm_source %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
write_csv(emm_time, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_emmeans_editing_time.csv"))
write_csv(emm_source, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_emmeans_source_by_modification.csv"))
```

# 9. Equivalence tests

```{r equivalence-helpers}
# An equivalence test by two one-sided tests asks whether an effect lies
# inside a bound of plus or minus b. One test asks whether the estimate is
# above -b, the other whether it is below +b, each at .05. Both pass exactly
# when the 90 percent confidence interval lies inside the bound, and the
# equivalence p-value is the larger of the two one-sided p-values. Degrees of
# freedom are Satterthwaite's, taken from emmeans.
tost <- function(est, se, df, bound, alpha = 0.05) {
  p_lower <- pt((est + bound) / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_upper <- pt((est - bound) / se, df, lower.tail = TRUE)
  crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  tibble(bound = bound, ci90_lo = est - crit * se, ci90_hi = est + crit * se,
         tost_p = pmax(p_lower, p_upper), equivalent = pmax(p_lower, p_upper) < alpha)
}

# The registered reading. An effect is called absent or small only if the
# equivalence test passes. A test neither significant nor equivalent is
# inconclusive.
equivalence_verdict <- function(significant, equivalent) {
  case_when(
    is.na(significant) | is.na(equivalent) ~ NA_character_,
    significant & !equivalent  ~ "significant, not inside the bound",
    significant & equivalent   ~ "significant and inside the bound",
    !significant & equivalent  ~ "absent or small: inside the bound",
    TRUE                       ~ "inconclusive: neither significant nor equivalent"
  )
}

# A contrast between estimated marginal means, with its two-sided test.
contrast_frame <- function(res, spec, weights, label) {
  ct <- emmeans::contrast(emm_of(res, spec), setNames(list(weights), label))
  as.data.frame(summary(ct, infer = c(FALSE, TRUE))) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character))
}
```

The two bounds are the ones set in section 1.3, before any model was fitted.

```{r equivalence}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_equivalence_editing_time.csv"),
                  file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_equivalence_source.csv"))
cat("Editing-time bound:", TIME_BOUND, "|", TIME_BOUND_SOURCE, "\n")
cat("Source bound:", SOURCE_BOUND, "\n")

# (a) Editing time, 100 hours minus less than 1 hour, on each rating. The
# significance half of the reading is the Holm verdict on the editing-time
# effect from section 7, the registered confirmatory test. The contrast's
# own two-sided p-value is reported beside it.
eq_time <- bind_rows(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) {
  res <- primary[[r]]
  if (!fit_usable(res$status)) {
    return(tibble(rating = r, note = fit_note(res$status, "test and the verdict")))
  }
  ct <- contrast_frame(res, ~ editing_time, c(-1, 0, 1),
                       "100 hours minus less than 1 hour")
  holm <- confirmatory %>% filter(rating == r, term == "editing_time")
  tibble(rating = r, contrast = ct$contrast, estimate = ct$estimate,
         se = ct$SE, df = ct$df, p_contrast = ct$p.value) %>%
    bind_cols(tost(ct$estimate, ct$SE, ct$df, TIME_BOUND)) %>%
    mutate(bound_source = TIME_BOUND_SOURCE,
           holm_significant = holm$holm_significant,
           verdict = equivalence_verdict(holm_significant, equivalent),
           pass_means = "smaller than Study 3's effect, not zero",
           note = "")
}))
print(as.data.frame(eq_time %>% select(rating, estimate, ci90_lo, ci90_hi, bound,
                                       tost_p, equivalent, holm_significant,
                                       verdict) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))

# (b) Source, Human minus AI at each modification level, on each rating.
# The registration names no correction for these nine tests, so the
# significance half is the contrast's own two-sided test at .05.
eq_source <- bind_rows(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) {
  res <- primary[[r]]
  if (!fit_usable(res$status)) {
    return(tibble(rating = r, note = fit_note(res$status, "test and the verdict")))
  }
  ct <- contrast_frame(res, ~ source | modification, c(1, -1), "Human minus AI")
  tibble(rating = r, modification = ct$modification, contrast = ct$contrast,
         estimate = ct$estimate, se = ct$SE, df = ct$df, p_contrast = ct$p.value) %>%
    bind_cols(tost(ct$estimate, ct$SE, ct$df, SOURCE_BOUND)) %>%
    mutate(significant = p_contrast < .05,
           verdict = equivalence_verdict(significant, equivalent),
           pass_means = "less than half of Study 1's creativity penalty reaches the second work",
           note = "")
}))
stopifnot(nrow(eq_source) == 9, nrow(eq_time) == 3)
print(as.data.frame(eq_source %>% select(rating, modification, estimate, ci90_lo,
                                         ci90_hi, tost_p, equivalent, p_contrast,
                                         verdict) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
write_csv(eq_time, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_equivalence_editing_time.csv"))
write_csv(eq_source, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_equivalence_source.csv"))
```

# 10. Cumulative-link checks of each Holm verdict

```{r clmm}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_clmm_fit_status.csv"),
                  file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_clmm_holm_check.csv"))

# A cumulative-link mixed model treats the five answers as ordered
# categories and estimates where the cut points between neighbouring answers
# fall, instead of treating the answers as evenly spaced numbers. The model
# has the same fixed and random terms and the same sum-to-zero coding as the
# linear model. Each of the six terms is tested by a Wald test, which
# compares the term's coefficients with their estimated covariance and gives
# a chi-square statistic with as many degrees of freedom as the term has
# columns. Holm's method corrects the six together, and each verdict is
# compared with the linear model's.
#
# The fit uses the clmm defaults, the Laplace approximation and the nlminb
# optimizer. A fit converged when the optimizer reported success and raised
# no warning about convergence or the Hessian (the matrix of second
# derivatives the standard errors come from). A fit is singular when a
# random-effect standard deviation is below 1e-4. These are Study 1's rules.
fit_clmm <- function(d) {
  d$rating_ord <- factor(d$rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE)
  f <- stats::as.formula(paste0("rating_ord ~ ", FIXED, " + (1 | id) + (1 | image)"))
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(ordinal::clmm(f, data = d, link = "logit", Hess = TRUE,
                           contrasts = SUM_CONTRASTS),
             error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  failed <- inherits(fit, "error")
  singular <- if (failed) NA else {
    any(vapply(ordinal::VarCorr(fit), function(m) any(attr(m, "stddev") < 1e-4),
               logical(1)))
  }
  list(fit = fit, data = d,
       status = tibble(
         fit_error = failed,
         converged = !failed && isTRUE(fit$optRes$convergence == 0) &&
           !any(grepl("converge|Hessian", warns, ignore.case = TRUE)),
         singular = singular,
         max_abs_gradient = if (failed) NA_real_ else max(abs(fit$gradient)),
         messages = paste(c(if (failed) conditionMessage(fit) else fit$optRes$message,
                            warns), collapse = " | ")))
}

wald_term <- function(res, term) {
  mm <- model.matrix(stats::as.formula(paste("~", FIXED)), data = res$data,
                     contrasts.arg = SUM_CONTRASTS)
  labels <- attr(terms(stats::as.formula(paste("~", FIXED))), "term.labels")
  cols <- colnames(mm)[attr(mm, "assign") == match(term, labels)]
  stopifnot(length(cols) > 0, all(cols %in% names(res$fit$beta)))
  b <- res$fit$beta[cols]
  V <- as.matrix(vcov(res$fit))[cols, cols, drop = FALSE]
  chisq <- as.numeric(t(b) %*% solve(V, b))
  tibble(chisq = chisq, df = length(cols),
         p = pchisq(chisq, length(cols), lower.tail = FALSE))
}

clmm_fits <- setNames(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) fit_clmm(primary_data(r))), RATINGS)
clmm_status <- bind_rows(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) {
  tibble(rating = r, n_obs = nrow(clmm_fits[[r]]$data), clmm_fits[[r]]$status)
}))
print(as.data.frame(clmm_status %>% select(-messages)))

clmm_check <- bind_rows(lapply(RATINGS, function(r) {
  res <- clmm_fits[[r]]
  usable <- !res$status$fit_error && res$status$converged
  bind_rows(lapply(names(FAMILY_TERMS), function(term) {
    w <- if (res$status$fit_error) tibble(chisq = NA_real_, df = NA_integer_, p = NA_real_)
         else wald_term(res, term)
    tibble(rating = r, term = term, test = unname(FAMILY_TERMS[term]),
           clmm_chisq = w$chisq, clmm_df = w$df,
           clmm_p_raw = if (usable) w$p else NA_real_,
           clmm_converged = res$status$converged, clmm_singular = res$status$singular,
           note = if (usable) "" else "fit errored or did not converge, so the p-value is set to NA")
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(clmm_p_holm = p.adjust(clmm_p_raw, method = "holm", n = 6),
         clmm_holm_significant = clmm_p_holm < .05) %>%
  left_join(confirmatory %>% select(rating, term, lmm_p_holm = p_holm,
                                    lmm_holm_significant = holm_significant),
            by = c("rating", "term")) %>%
  mutate(verdicts_agree = clmm_holm_significant == lmm_holm_significant)
stopifnot(nrow(clmm_check) == 6)
print(as.data.frame(clmm_check %>% select(rating, test, clmm_chisq, clmm_df,
                                          clmm_p_holm, clmm_holm_significant,
                                          lmm_holm_significant, verdicts_agree) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
write_csv(clmm_status, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_clmm_fit_status.csv"))
write_csv(clmm_check, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_clmm_holm_check.csv"))
```
